fields.briefDescription: Encrypted delivery, permanent version licenses, and approved creator revenue splits for locally installed Agent Skills, using Solana USDC escrow.
fields.buildingAndAudience: SkillSeal helps Agent developers publish and install reusable workflow packages with clear version licenses and creator shares. The live 0.2 website includes Creator Studio upload/preview, signed author approvals, operator file inspection, permanent version share pages, verified free ZIP delivery and a standalone CLI. Approved free Skills need no buyer account or wallet. The paid design uses encrypted packages and Solana USDC escrow to couple a wallet/version license with approved creator payouts atomically. Our MIT Research Brief turns supplied sources into a cited decision brief. Alibaba Cloud acceptance passed signed publication/review, exact ZIP/CLI installation and release/key persistence after app restart. The existing website stayed healthy. A public Devnet CLI purchase paid 0.7/0.3 test USDC and verified installation/recovery. Hosted paid checkout stays disabled; browser/refund checks remain pending. The service holds content keys and cannot prevent copying after decryption.
fields.whyAndWhyNow: Agent workflows increasingly combine prompts, reference material, and reusable instructions into locally installed packages. We want to test whether creators can sell those packages while preserving local use and sharing revenue with collaborators. SkillSeal focuses first on developers who already use wallets, rather than assuming every buyer wants crypto payments. Solana makes the approved split and wallet/version receipt inspectable, while encryption and the installer handle delivery. Ordinary payment systems can offer similar access control; our hypothesis is that wallet-native teams value transparent collaboration accounting and purchase recovery. We have not established paying demand. The next experiment is to observe a small group of developers purchasing and reinstalling a useful Skill, measure failures and total costs, and distinguish interest from actual payment commitments.
fields.technologies: Solana; Anchor/Rust escrow program; SPL Token and Devnet USDC; TypeScript; Next.js 16 and React 19; Node.js 24; SQLite; AES-256-GCM; libsodium X25519 sealed boxes; @solana/web3.js; Phantom/Solflare wallet integration; pnpm; GitHub Actions. OpenAI Codex assisted implementation, review, tests, and documentation. The current prototype does not require an LLM API to buy or install a Skill.
fields.chainUsage: The Anchor program registers immutable versions and approved author splits. It escrows Devnet USDC, then atomically records a wallet/version license and pays collaborators. The key service checks finalized state before delivery. Public Devnet deployment, both approvals, a 1 test-USDC CLI purchase, 70/30 payouts and recovery are verified. The contract supports buyer refunds after 600 seconds; browser-wallet and public refund checks remain pending.
